dedupe_keys.name: hanoi system and extended hanoi water distribution benchmark networks fujiwara and khang bi dandy and maier

description: The Hanoi network is a widely used water distribution design benchmark from Fujiwara and Khang (1990), and Extended Hanoi is the extended variant from Bi, Dandy and Maier (2015); Graeme Dandy contributed both to the Water Distribution System Research Database (entries 27 and 41). The Hanoi entry offers a description PDF and an EPANET zip; the Extended Hanoi entry offers an EPANET zip only; DataCite has DOIs for both. The summary spreadsheet gives 34 pipes, 31 nodes and one reservoir in a looped layout for each, with no pumps or tanks, and a demand of 126.54 million gallons per day. Coverage is the Hanoi supply zone as a design case, with no calibration. The files are free; the pages state no licence, only a copyright notice. Only the index page, the entry pages, the summary spreadsheet and DataCite metadata were read; no network file was downloaded or run. The networks serve pipe-sizing and cost-minimisation optimisation, multiobjective and evolutionary algorithm testing, and solver comparison. Related records: the leakage datasets for Hanoi and Anytown, EPANET, the database record and the New York Tunnels benchmark.
